correctness.rationale: For n>=7, every radius-two clique outside a consecutive-column slab contains a unique distance-two endpoint pair B_(j,a) in columns j-1,j+1 with equal C5 coordinate. Its remaining vertices form an arbitrary subset T of the three compatible middle-column vertices a-1,a,a+1. Uniqueness follows from column-span and n>=7, so the 5n disjoint eight-face families admit four codimension-one free-face pairs each, removing exactly 40n faces in 20n collapses. Each remaining two-column slab S_j is the independence complex of the forbidden cross-column C10 (not a matching): Ind(C10) ~= S^2 by the standard path/cycle independence-complex recurrence. Adjacent slab intersections are full five-vertex simplices and there are no nonadjacent or triple intersections. The homotopy pushout of this cyclic cover is S^1 wedge n copies of S^2. Inclusion-exclusion and removed faces give the full nonempty face vector (5n,30n,55n,35n,6n). Independent clique enumeration and exhaustive immediate-coface tests for n=7,8,9,10,11 confirmed all 20n collapses and remaining slabs; finite tests only corroborate the combinatorial uniform proof, not replace it.
